newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Arafat sees plot to "pulverise" peace process.
newsitem.headline: Arafat sees plot to "pulverise" peace process.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat on Tuesday accused Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of plotting to "pulverise" the Middle East peace process.
He told reporters after meeting Tunisian President Zine al-Abidine Ben Ali in Tunis:

"I have fully informed the president about the obstacles the Israeli prime minister is putting in the way of the peace process with the aim of freezing it. There is a plot to pulverise the peace process."

"The Netanyahu government wants to escape implementing Israel's commitments to the (PLO-Israel peace) accords signed at the White House under (U.S.) President Bill Clinton sponsorship," Arafat told a news conference a few hours later.
"The situation is very tense for the Palestinian people. There are clashes in Rafah, Hebron, Jebel Abu Gheneim, and Jerusalem," in the West Bank, Arafat said.
Israeli soldiers on Tuesday shot and wounded at least 35 Palestinians in another flareup of violence over posters depicting the Moslem Prophet Mohammad as a pig.
Israel police on Saturday arrested a 25-year-old Jewish woman on suspicion of pasting the posters on about 20 storefronts in Hebron.

"At a time settlers pasted these heinous posters...the Israeli army defends these settlers and opens fire against the Palestinian people and children," Arafat said while showing the poster to journalists.
Israeli-Palestinian peace moves ground to a halt in March after Israel starting building a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.

"Jerusalem is facing an Israeli attack to Judaise it. I appeal our Arab and Moslem nation to defend (East) Jerusalem because this is not only a Palestinian cause, but also an Arab, Moslem and Christian cause," he said.

Arafat said he will visit Egypt next Thursday for talks with President Hosni Mubarak for a "follow up" of the Egyptian efforts to have Israel and the PLO resume peace talks. "The Egyptian initiative is continuing," he said.
He said that, at the demand of the United States, a meeting between Palestinian, Israeli and U.S. security officials was held last Sunday.
Arafat didn't say where but he added that resuming PLO-Israeli security coordination was linked to the peace talks themselves.
He said a secret meeting last week between PLO's number two, Mahmoud Abbas, alias Abu Mazen, and Israeli National Infrastructure Minister Ariel Sharon was unfruitful.
"I regret, it didn't lead to any tangible result so far," he said.
Arafat was due to visit Algiers on Wednesday before heading to Cairo. He said he also plans to visit Britain, but did not say when.
